channel.title: The Brussels Times
channel.description: Latest Brussels posts from The Brussels Times.

item.title: One third of Brussels healthcare facilities overexposed to NO₂
item.description: “It would be a scandal to find cyanide in paracetamol. So why do we accept breathing in nitrogen dioxide at concentrations that are hazardous to health in the vicinity of our hospitals?"

item.title: 'Symbol of submission': Brussels secretary claims to be fired over privately worn headscarf
item.description: A woman has taken the City of Brussels to the labour tribunal, alleging that municipal bosses fired her because she wears an Islamic headscarf outside work.

item.title: 120 take part in ‘Sing/Fuck the Planet’ protest in Brussels
item.description: The protest called for stronger climate justice and more ambitious policy in the run-up to the COP31 conference to be held in Türkiye.

item.title: Young man killed by telehandler in Brussels
item.description: Authorities believe the telehandler had been used by several young people during the night before the incident.

item.title: Infamous Anderlecht drug gang to go to court on Monday
item.description: 45 people are suspected of participating in the Peterbos drug ring.

item.title: US ambassador to Belgium outraged by Brussels synagogue attack
item.description: Bill White visited the synagogue in Anderlecht on Saturday with Israel’s ambassador to Belgium, David Saranga, after the building was targeted in what White called a clear act of antisemitic vandalism.

item.title: Brussels students end university campus occupation after two weeks
item.description: Students occupied the P1 building of the Solbosch campus as an act of soldarity towards their 12 peers stuck in Palestine after having their visas rejected.

item.title: 25 years without flagship Belgian airline Sabena
item.description: Sabena's collapse remains one of Belgium's biggest industrial shocks.

item.title: Cinemamed film festival line-up announced
item.description: “What interests us most are the subjects and the discussions sparked by the films.”

item.title: Brussels residents mobilise against plans for 7,000-grave multi-faith cemetery
item.description: Residents of Berchem-Sainte-Agathe and Molenbeek-Saint-Jean are joining forces to oppose plans for a new multi-faith cemetery on the Hoogveld site.

item.title: What to do in Brussels this weekend: 6 - 8 November
item.description: From Indian food and guided architecture tours to becoming a forester or immersing yourself in Asian cultures, there is something for everyone.

item.title: Navigating essential public services in Brussels for English speakers
item.description: Upon arrival to Brussels, international residents are told that daily life is easy to navigate in English. But this is not necessarily always true.

item.title: Dutch beauty brand Marie-Stella-Maris expands in Brussels as Belgian demand grows
item.description: The brand's CEO highlighted differences between Belgian and Dutch shopping habits, describing Belgian customers as more considered in their choices.

item.title: Brussels Region no longer at yellow alert for drought
item.description: Rainfall in recent weeks, particularly the severe storm on 24 October, has helped bring the situation partly back to normal.

item.title: 'Transforming what's already there': Brussels building named world's best high-rise
item.description: The building was described as "a paradigm shift in high-rise construction," putting transformation, resource efficiency and mixed use ahead of demolition and new build.

item.title: Brussels collects €6 million in fines from illegal Airbnb rentals
item.description: The Brussels-Capital Region is expected to collect around €6 million in fines from unregistered Airbnb properties by the end of 2026, following a major crackdown on illegal short-term rentals.

item.title: Growing share of sellers in Brussels offloading apartments that need renovation work
item.description: Brussels' energy performance rules are pushing many homeowners to sell properties that need renovation, even if it means a lower price.

item.title: Former Schaerbeek city councillor De Herde to appear in court on suspicion of rape
item.description: Former Schaerbeek city councillor Michel De Herde (ex-DéFI), suspected of raping several victims, is due to appear in court in March 2027.

item.title: New data centre in Brussels to account for 3% of region’s total electricity consumption
item.description: "Every Megawatt of grid capacity allocated to these servers is capacity that can no longer be used for a hospital, a tram depot, or an electric vehicle charging station."

item.title: Belgian fixed term energy contracts have climbed €1,400 since March
item.description: In Brussels, the average unit price for gas has more than doubled, moving from 5.47 c€/kWh in March to 11.47 c€/kWh now.
